askSize: If the user gave no size, do not ask: scan at the default size, 1,000 USD unless the user changed it. Name the size in the first sentence of the reply (`sizeUsd` in the result), and offer a re-rank at 5,000 or 25,000 USD in the closing You can.
askOwner: If owner is unset, use AskUserQuestion to ask for the public wallet address (it starts with 0x); say to type it in, and never name the free-text option, whose label varies by version. Never ask for a key. Wait for the address, then use it with `--owner`. Do not change config unless the user explicitly asks to save it.
askWallet: If owner is unset, use AskUserQuestion: "Which wallet do you want to use?" with four choices: "Bring my browser wallet" (MetaMask, Rabby), "Bring my wallet into mstack's encrypted keystore", "Create a new wallet with mstack", and "Bring my phone wallet (WalletConnect)" (needs a free Reown project id). For a browser or phone wallet, ask for its public 0x address; for a phone wallet, the human gets a free project id at https://cloud.reown.com and saves it in their own terminal with `mob config set walletconnect_project_id` and the id. For a keystore choice, the human runs `mob keystore import` (existing key) or `mob keystore create` (new key) in a separate terminal window, never in this chat, and replies with the address it prints. A created wallet starts empty; its keystore file (`~/.mob/keystore` by default) and passphrase are the only copy: the human backs up both and funds the wallet on each venue. Never ask for or accept a private key, seed phrase, or passphrase in the chat. Pass the address with `--owner`; `mob onboard` saves it only once setup is staged.
askOpen: Use AskUserQuestion for each missing choice. Wait for the answer before staging.
askSign: Use AskUserQuestion with the choice that fits the user's wallet, then "Reject <id>": browser wallet, "Sign <id> in the browser wallet"; phone wallet, "Sign <id> with WalletConnect"; keystore wallet, "Sign <id> in my approver terminal" when `mob hello --json` reports `approver.running`, else "I will sign <id> myself in my terminal with the keystore". The wallet comes from this conversation or `mob config get signer`; if neither says, offer every way. Put the staged id in place of <id> in every choice. Only a chosen label that starts with Sign <id> authorizes. Run the matching command with a ten-minute tool timeout: `mob sign <id> --with browser`, `mob sign <id> --with walletconnect`, or `mob sign <id> --with approver`. For the keystore choice, stop and tell the human to run `mob sign <id> --with keystore` in their own terminal.
askSubmit: Use AskUserQuestion with these choices: "Submit <id> now" / "Reject <id>". Replace <id> with the staged Proposal id in both choices. The chosen label is the authorization; run the submit only after a label that starts with Submit <id>.
askTrade: Trading runs through MoB with a scoped API key the user controls: it has venue and USD caps, cannot withdraw, and can be revoked at any time. Use AskUserQuestion: "Trading runs through MoB. Set it up now? One wallet session, about five minutes." with two choices: "Set up MoB trading now" / "Not now, keep researching". Ask only this and stop; add nothing after the question. Only after "Set up MoB trading now", load `/mob-setup` and follow it. After "Not now", offer a scan, funding history, or an explanation, and do not bring up setup again until the user asks to trade.
askMenu: use AskUserQuestion with one question, "What do you want to do?" followed by the first of those two sentences, header "mstack", and one option per entry of `sections` in `mob menu --json`, in order: the label is the section `name`, the description is its `note`, and the `preview` is a fenced code block with the `note` on its first line, a blank line, then the welcome lines verbatim. The host collapses tool output and may show no text before a question, so the preview is where the user sees the welcome. When the user picks a section, use AskUserQuestion again with one question that names the section, header "mstack", and one option per row of that section, in order: the label is the row's `say` words and the description is its `about`. When the chosen row has `pick`, use AskUserQuestion a third time with one question, "Which asset?", header "mstack", and one option per entry of `assets`: the label is its `ticker` and the description its `name`. Put the chosen ticker, or the free text behind "Other", in place of `<asset>` in `pick`. Treat those words, the chosen row label, or the free text behind "Other" in any question, as the user's own words: load the skill for it and follow it. If AskUserQuestion is not available in this session, list the sections and their rows as numbered lines instead, and end the reply with the question.
